title: Findings
description: What a lens is allowed to say. Everything a lens produces passes through this shape, and two mechanical guards are built into it: a finding must quote code that literally exists (file, line, snippet) and it must be reproducible (inputs, consequence). A finding that cannot fill those in is not a finding.

findings.description: Empty is a valid and common answer. Do not invent a finding to fill this.

file.description: Repository-relative path, exactly as the repository spells it.

line.description: 1-indexed line in the file at head where the defect lives.

snippet.description: The code itself, copied verbatim from the file. It is checked by exact search near `line`, so it must be quoted, not paraphrased or reconstructed from memory.

inputs.description: The concrete inputs or state that trigger the defect. "an empty items list", "a video with no captions and duration_s = 0". Not "certain conditions".

consequence.description: What observably goes wrong with those inputs. "raises IndexError", "writes a card with an empty summary". Not "could cause problems".

glossary.correctness: the code computes or returns the wrong thing for some reachable input
glossary.boundary: empty, zero, one, maximum, off-by-one, or an unhandled edge of a range
glossary.contract: an interface used against its documented or implied terms: wrong type, wrong order, ignored error, broken invariant
glossary.resource: something acquired and not released, or growing without bound: handles, memory, connections, unbounded retries or cost
glossary.test-quality: a test that cannot fail, asserts the wrong property, or freezes current behaviour as if it were intended

glossary.introduced: the change creates the defect: before it, the code did not have it
glossary.exposed: the defect was already in the code, and the change makes it reachable, visible or more likely
glossary.pre-existing: the defect was already in the code, and the change has no bearing on it

glossary.blocking: merging this ships a defect that reaches users or corrupts data
glossary.significant: a real defect on a reachable path, but bounded - degraded, recoverable, or behind a rare condition
glossary.minor: real but low impact: cosmetic, or a path that is hard to reach
